tools.name: check_eol
tools.description: Check whether a specific version of a software product is end-of-life (EOL). Returns lifecycle status, the EOL date, days remaining or days past EOL, the latest release, and eol_date_source (where the date comes from: vendor-override, vendor-fetched, vendor-verified, custom, upstream, or discrepancy

tools.name: get_risk_score
tools.description: Get the proprietary EOL Risk Score (0-100) for a product version, with the four-factor breakdown (EOL recency, attack surface, CISA KEV exposure, extended support). Omit "version" to score the product's highest-risk (most recently end-of-lifed) release. Use this to quantify how dangerous it is to ke

tools.name: scan_stack
tools.description: Audit a whole stack at once. Provide a list of products (optionally with versions) — e.g. parsed from a package.json or Dockerfile — and get an EOL Risk Score for each, so you can see what is unsupported and dangerous in one call. For CycloneDX or SPDX documents use check_sbom instead. Free tier: up

tools.name: list_products
tools.description: List or search the products endoflife.ai tracks (500+). Pass an optional "query" substring to find the canonical slug for a product before calling the other tools (e.g. "postgres" → "postgresql"). Returns matching product slugs.

tools.name: get_product_lifecycle
tools.description: Get the full version history for one product: every tracked version/cycle with its release date, EOL date, support status, and EOL Risk Score. Use for "give me the whole EOL schedule for X".

tools.name: get_kev_exposure
tools.description: The exploited-vulnerability record for a product: every CVE CISA lists against it in the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, with the date added, the federal due date and CISA's required-action text verbatim (the "discontinue use" entries are the ones that matter for end-of-life versions), plus

tools.name: get_upcoming_eol
tools.description: What reaches end-of-life soon. Returns every tracked version whose EOL date falls within the next N days (default 90), optionally limited to a list of products, sorted by date. Also lists versions that went EOL within the last "recent_past_days" days when set. Use for "what in our stack expires this

tools.name: get_edge_device_status
tools.description: Query the EOS Edge Device Intelligence feed — firewalls, VPN gateways and appliances, ADCs, router and switch operating systems — with end-of-support status in the vocabulary of CISA BOD 26-02 (eos, within-12-months, scheduled, no-date-announced). Filter by platform or vendor name, by status, or by

tools.name: get_upgrade_path
tools.description: Where to move a product version: the current version's support status and score, the supported releases with the longest remaining support, endoflife.ai's recommended target, and the vendor's stated successor where one is published (edge appliances). Use after check_eol says a version is EOL.

tools.name: check_sbom
tools.description: Audit a CycloneDX or SPDX JSON software bill of materials. Components are mapped to tracked products and scored for EOL risk; unmatched components are listed honestly rather than guessed. Pass the SBOM as a JSON string or object. Free tier scores up to 5 matched components per call; Pro up to 50.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "list_products" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: List or search the products endoflife.ai tracks (500+). Pass an optional "query" substring to find the canonical slug for a product before calling the other too…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "check_eol" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
